title: A complete set of polymerases that synthesize in the 3′-to-5′ direction

concept.text: Millennium Problems for Biology 11, 5′ polymerases. Target: a complete set of polymerases acting in the 3′ to 5′ direction (DNA polymerase, RNA polymerase, reverse transcriptase and RNA-dependent RNA polymerase) with processivity and error rates matching or exceeding Taq, T7 RNA polymerase, M-MLV reverse transcriptase and Phi 6 RdRP. Sources given: https://millenniumproblems.bio/.

change_log.change: Added by hand to BCH on 2026-11-15.
change_log.reason: One of the twelve Millennium Problems for Biology (Sam Rodriques and Michaela Hinks, FutureHouse and Edison Scientific, 2026), each with a stated concrete target; added at the owner's request, November 14, 2026.

page.title: A complete set of 3′–5′ polymerases
page.definition: Protein polymerases copy a template by adding nucleotides to the product strand’s 5′ end, so the product grows 3′→5′. Either DNA or RNA can serve as the template for either a DNA or an RNA product, giving four template→product combinations. Thg1-like proteins already perform one of these activities on model RNA strands, where a separate RNA template has directed the addition of up to eight nucleotides.

goal.need: Laboratories that need RNA with an exact 5′ end face a constraint when they make it by transcription. On two tested templates specifying an initial C or U, T7 RNA polymerase skipped that base and began at the next G. Conventional polymerases extend an existing strand only at its 3′ end. Copying a guide at the 5′ end would let a laboratory add a chosen sequence or a fluorescent tag to RNA it already has, without joining two preformed strands. This requires a guide that pairs with the RNA and an enzyme that accepts the intended sequence.

statements.quote: Produce a full set of polymerases that act in the 5′ direction.
Each problem is intended to be very difficult to solve, but easy to validate in a simple laboratory environment.
statements.context: The announcement published on 23 September 2026 introduces twelve challenges, including 5′ polymerases.

completion.title: All four 3′–5′ polymerase classes have processivity and error characteristics similar or superior to their comparators.
completion.criterion: Demonstrate 3′–5′ synthesis for all four template→product combinations. Compare DNA→DNA with Taq DNA polymerase, DNA→RNA with T7 RNA polymerase, RNA→DNA with M-MLV reverse transcriptase, and RNA→RNA with Phi 6 RNA-dependent RNA polymerase. For each pair, demonstrate similar or superior processivity and copying error characteristics.
completion.set_by: FutureHouse and Edison Scientific, Millennium Problems for Biology, problem 11.
completion.threshold_quote: processivity and error characteristics that are similar to or superior to those of Taq, T7 RNA pol, M-MLV RT, and Phi 6 RDRP respectively.
completion.basis: Problem 11 names a comparator for each activity. It leaves the measurement methods, the error characteristics to report and the numerical meaning of “similar” unspecified. Processivity describes how many nucleotides an enzyme adds in one binding event.

milestones.title: An enzyme adds a template-directed nucleotide to a nucleic acid’s 5′ end.
milestones.criterion: For the case’s template and product, demonstrate enzyme-catalysed addition of at least one complementary nucleotide to the 5′ end of the product strand through a standard phosphodiester bond. Identify the template, the strand extended and the nucleotide incorporated so that the template and product chemistries can be assigned.
milestones.set_by: Atlas. No external body specifies a single-addition milestone across the four classes.

milestones.title: An enzyme adds at least two templated nucleotides to a primer’s 5′ end using a separate template.
milestones.criterion: For the case’s template/product combination, demonstrate that a separate template strand directs at least two successive, complementary nucleotide additions to the 5′ end of the same primer.
milestones.set_by: Atlas. Two successive additions distinguish repeated extension from single-nucleotide transfer. No external body specifies an intermediate count.

milestones.title: A 3′–5′ polymerase has processivity similar or superior to its class comparator’s.
milestones.criterion: For one template/product combination, compare the number of nucleotides added per enzyme-binding event with the corresponding forward polymerase under comparable measurements. Demonstrate similar or superior processivity, distinguishing extension during one binding event from extension after rebinding.
milestones.set_by: Atlas defines the intermediate stage. Its performance comparison comes from FutureHouse and Edison Scientific’s problem 11, which gives no separate processivity qualification protocol.
milestones.threshold_quote: processivity and error characteristics that are similar to or superior to those of Taq, T7 RNA pol, M-MLV RT, and Phi 6 RDRP respectively.

milestones.title: One 3′–5′ polymerase class meets both comparisons for processivity and copying errors.
milestones.criterion: For one template/product combination, demonstrate that the same 3′–5′ polymerase has both processivity and copying error characteristics similar or superior to those of the forward comparator named for that class.
milestones.set_by: Atlas tracks each class separately. FutureHouse and Edison Scientific’s problem 11 specifies both comparisons for each class and defines completion for the full set.
milestones.threshold_quote: processivity and error characteristics that are similar to or superior to those of Taq, T7 RNA pol, M-MLV RT, and Phi 6 RDRP respectively.

not_found: Searches found no numerical definition of “similar”, prescribed assay, sequence panel or acceptance statistics for problem 11.
Searches found no externally adopted staged roadmap or qualification protocol for the complete reverse-polymerase set.
Searches found no experimental demonstration of DNA-templated 3′–5′ DNA or RNA synthesis.
Searches found no complete set, or individual reverse-polymerase class, tested against both of its specified comparator characteristics.
No estimate was found of the number of laboratories, experiments or costs affected by the lack of the complete set.
No statement from a scientific society or roadmap committee was found disputing the value or feasibility of the four-class goal.

results.detail: Single-turnover incorporation efficiencies bear on fidelity, but do not establish errors per copied nucleotide or retain a comparator-level processivity result.

results.finding: AcaTLP2, in a seven-enzyme screen, added 1 complementary C to the RNA primer’s 5′ end.
results.detail: The gel resolved the single-C product when CTP was the only incoming nucleotide. The paper assigns the linkage from the reaction chemistry.
results.quote: The reaction with GTP omitted also allowed us to identify the band corresponding to the first CTP addition

results.finding: DdiTLP4 added 8 templated nucleotides to the RNA primer’s 5′ end in the major product across five duplex designs.
results.detail: Both enzymes fully extended the alternating G/C template. The authors could not distinguish template repositioning from nontemplated addition in AcaTLP2 products that extended beyond the designed overhang.
results.quote: Again, DdiTLP4 extended each substrate with a major product that corresponds to the expected 8-nt addition, although the overall efficiency of extension appeared to improve with shorter duplexes.

results.finding: Yeast SceThg1 showed kinetic base-substitution fidelity of 10⁻¹ to 10⁻⁶ across 16 NTP–tRNA pairings, with at least three independent assays per pairing.
results.detail: The fidelity range comes from ratios of catalytic efficiencies for individual additions. The assay did not count copying errors in extended RNA products or measure nucleotides added per binding event.

results.finding: PaThg1 added a complementary C to the 5′ end of truncated E. coli tRNA^His in 8 of 25 sequenced products.
results.detail: The sequencing reaction used guide 1 alone with all four ribonucleotides. The template was part of the same RNA molecule.
results.quote: Eight sequences encoded an additional C, which represents a single nucleotide repair.
